propositions: Blocking-link comparability was keyed on TYPE_TIER instead of structural position in the parent hierarchy, allowing tickets of different types but same parent to be rejected and silently escalated to a higher level.

Ancestor-blocking edges (a ticket blocking its own parent or ancestor) could be recorded under the type-tier rule, distorting ready/next-batch scheduling and breaking the parent-first cascade invariant.
The redirect record for auto-escalated cross-subtree links is discarded on the rebar.link() library path because quiet mode sinks stdout/stderr, leaving callers unaware of the substitution.

Existing legacy edges written under the old type-tier rule must be detected store-wide and repairable in a single pass without breaking the escalation contract or silent-substitution behaviour on the MCP path.
